page: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC processors on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 1280 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-threaded capabilities alongside moderate single-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, cached read-only memory bandwidth, and Passmark CPU extended instruction and encryption tests. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation with clang, register strong performance. Conversely, single-threaded tasks show limitations, with gzip compression scoring in the lower tier and Geekbench single-core results falling in the average range.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high compute density with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a cost-efficient option for highly parallelized workloads that do not require massive per-core memory allocations. The primary tradeoff is the moderate 2.0 GHz clock speed, which limits single-threaded execution speed in favor of massive parallel throughput. This profile is highly suitable for multi-threaded workloads, including software compilation, parallel data decompression, cryptography, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 96 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs (48 physical cores), 256.0 GB of RAM, and 1280 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and high cached memory bandwidth, though single-threaded performance remains average due to a 2.0 GHz clock speed. With a resource ratio of 2.67 GB of RAM per core, it represents a dense compute configuration. This instance is well-suited for highly parallelized workloads such as software compilation, cryptography, multi-threaded data processing, and high-throughput web serving.
